synopsis: Terrain and soil tools model ground deformation, digging and loose-material flow because soft ground changes machine stopping; semi-empirical terramechanics can predict braking force and sinkage [f15981, f6461]. Across the booklet, the market is modular: heavy-machine tools offer strong terrain and hydraulics but thin sensor and scenario tooling, and combining separate renderer, dynamics, soil and HIL tools requires high integration effort [f195, f8283, f15860, f13240]. Available methods range from fast Bekker-Wong SCM to grain-based DEM and continuum SPH/CRM; Project Chrono 10.0.0, dated 27 March 2026, supports wheeled, tracked and articulated vehicles on deformable terrain [f15982, f15983, f15984, f8301]. High fidelity is not suitable for broad scenario sweeps: Chrono continuum soil simulation runs 50–200 times slower than real time, while uncertain soil inputs can overwhelm the benefit of model fidelity [f15992, f16233, f15993]. The recommended approach is to use detailed terrain simulation to characterize stopping-distance sensitivity to soil, slope and payload, fit simpler models for regression testing, and confirm the parameter envelope through targeted physical tests [f15994].
